column2: The manager's anecdote about one delighted customer made a nice story but proved nothing about overall satisfaction.
column3: 經理講的那位滿意顧客的軼事是個好故事，卻無法證明整體滿意度。
column5: anecdote 像「俺可得」：俺可得講個小故事，卻不是證據

column2: Anecdotal reports of faster delivery are encouraging, but the company has not measured delivery times.
column3: 關於送貨變快的傳聞式回報令人鼓舞，但公司並未實際測量送貨時間。
column5: anecdote 加 al：只靠一兩個故事，不是正式數據

column2: Empirical studies of retail pricing rely on real transaction records rather than on theoretical models alone.
column3: 零售定價的實證研究依賴真實交易紀錄，而不是只靠理論模型。
column5: em 在裡面 + peiria 試驗：親自下場做實驗才算數

column2: Quantitative analysis of two thousand receipts revealed that most customers bought only one item per visit.
column3: 對兩千張收據的量化分析顯示，多數顧客每次只買一件商品。
column5: quant 像 quantity 數量：用數字說話

column2: Qualitative interviews with ten shoppers uncovered feelings about the brand that no spreadsheet could capture.
column3: 對十位購物者的質性訪談，揭露了試算表無法捕捉的品牌感受。
column5: quality 品質 + ative：看的是感受與品質，不是數字

column2: The court's ruling set a precedent that later disputes over exclusive supplier contracts would follow.
column3: 法院的判決樹立了先例，日後關於獨家供應商合約的爭議都會依循。
column5: pre 之前 + cede 走：先走過的那個腳印

column2: The pandemic caused an unprecedented drop in air travel, with no earlier crisis coming close.
column3: 疫情造成航空旅運史無前例的下滑，先前沒有任何危機能與之相比。
column4: an unprecedented increase (史無前例的增長)
column5: un 沒有 + precedent 先例：前面沒有人走過

column2: The consultant drew an analogy between a firm's cash flow and blood circulating through a body.
column3: 顧問把公司的現金流比作在身體中循環的血液。
column5: ana 對照 + logy 說法：拿熟悉的事來說明陌生的事

column2: Launching a phone in a new country is analogous to opening a franchise in an unfamiliar city.
column3: 在新的國家推出手機，類似於在陌生城市開設加盟店。
column5: analogy 的形容詞：兩件事像一對雙胞胎

column2: Extrapolation from three quarters of rapid growth to a decade of the same is a risky forecast.
column3: 把三個季度的快速成長外推成十年的相同成長，是一種冒險的預測。
column5: extra 外面 + polate：把線往外多畫延長

column2: Arrange the product launches in chronological order, beginning with the oldest model released in 1998.
column3: 請依時間先後排列產品發表，從一九九八年發行的最舊款式開始。
column5: chrono 像 clock 時鐘：照時鐘先後順序排好

column2: The auditor built a chronology of every transaction made between March and June to find the error.
column3: 稽核員建立了三月至六月間每筆交易的年代順序紀錄，以找出錯誤。
column4: a detailed chronology (詳細的大事年表)
column5: chrono 時間 + logy 記錄：把事情按時間記錄成表

column2: The temporal order of events matters: the price cut came first, and only afterward did sales rise.
column3: 事件的時間順序很重要：先降價，之後銷售才上升。
column5: temp 像 tempo 節拍：和時間先後有關的

column2: The apparent link between umbrella sales and traffic jams is spurious; heavy rain causes both.
column3: 雨傘銷量與塞車之間表面上的關聯是虛假的，因為大雨同時造成兩者。
column5: spurious 像「是不是歐斯」：看起來有關，其實是假的

column2: Age is a confounder in the study, since older patients both take the drug and recover more slowly.
column3: 年齡是這項研究中的混雜因素，因為年紀較大的患者既服用該藥，恢復也較慢。
column4: control for a confounder (控制混雜因素)
column5: confound 搞混 + er：把兩種原因攪成一團的攪局者

column2: Bonus payments should be proportional to sales, so that a manager earns twice as much for doubling results.
column3: 獎金應與銷售額成正比，使經理的成績加倍時獎金也加倍。
column5: pro 對 + portion 份：一份對一份，成比例

column2: A disproportionate share of the profit came from a few products, while hundreds of others lost money.
column3: 利潤中有不成比例的大部分來自少數產品，而數百種其他產品都在虧錢。
column4: a disproportionate share (不成比例的份額)
column5: dis 不 + proportionate：蹺蹺板一邊太重，比例歪掉

column2: Demand and price share an inverse relationship: as the price climbs, the quantity bought tends to fall.
column3: 需求與價格呈反向關係：價格上漲，購買量往往下降。
column5: in 向內 + verse 轉：一邊升，另一邊就倒過來降

column2: In a linear model, each extra hour of training adds exactly the same increase in output.
column3: 在線性模型中，每多一小時訓練，產出就增加完全相同的量。
column5: line 直線 + ar：畫成圖是一條筆直的線

column2: Growth that starts slowly and then explodes is nonlinear, so a straight-line forecast would badly underestimate it.
column3: 起初緩慢而後爆發的成長是非線性的，所以直線預測會嚴重低估。
column5: non 不 + linear 直線：畫出來彎彎曲曲的曲線

column2: The probability of rain tomorrow is eighty percent, so the outdoor sale will probably be cancelled.
column3: 明天下雨的機率是百分之八十，所以戶外特賣會大概會取消。
column5: probable 很可能 + ity：事情發生的可能有多大

column2: Insurers use probabilistic models, which estimate chances rather than promise exact outcomes for any single customer.
column3: 保險公司使用機率模型，估計可能性，而不是為任何單一客戶保證確切結果。
column5: probability 機率 + istic：說的是可能性，不是保證

column2: Location is the main determinant of a restaurant's success, outweighing menu quality and price.
column3: 地點是餐廳成功的關鍵決定因素，比菜單品質與價格更重要。
column4: a key determinant (關鍵決定因素)
column5: determine 決定 + ant：那個一錘定音的決定者

column2: A pilot test will determine whether customers actually prefer the new packaging to the old design.
column3: 一項試辦測試將查明顧客是否真的偏好新包裝勝過舊設計。
column5: de 完全 + termin 界線：把界線劃清楚，事情就定了

column2: About half of the revenue drop is attributable to the factory closure in the spring.
column3: 營收下降大約有一半可歸因於春季的工廠關閉。
column5: attribute 歸因 + able：責任可以掛在某個原因頭上

column2: Analysts attribute the company's recovery to a leaner supply chain rather than to any new product.
column3: 分析師將公司的復甦歸因於更精簡的供應鏈，而非任何新產品。
column4: attribute success to (把成功歸因於)
column5: at 向 + tribute 給：把功勞或責任遞給某個原因

column2: Historians ascribe the firm's early success to cheap labor, though other factors probably mattered too.
column3: 歷史學家將該公司早期的成功歸因於廉價勞工，不過其他因素可能也很重要。
column4: ascribe it to luck (歸因於運氣)
column5: a 向 + scribe 寫：把原因寫在某人名字底下

column2: The plausibility of the theory improved once a second independent study produced similar results.
column3: 當第二項獨立研究得出相似結果後，這個理論的可信度提高了。
column5: plausible 的名詞：聽起來有多讓人想相信

column2: The auditor's working presumption was that every receipt was genuine until something suggested otherwise.
column3: 稽核員的工作推定是，除非出現相反的跡象，否則每張收據都是真的。
column5: pre 先 + sume 取：還沒證明，先拿來當真

column2: Investors presume that audited accounts are accurate, which is why a hidden error shocks the market.
column3: 投資人假定經過查核的帳目是準確的，所以隱藏的錯誤才會震驚市場。
column5: pre 先 + sume 取：先假設是真的，再往下走

column2: Under the presumptive rule, a new product is assumed profitable until the sales data show otherwise.
column3: 依據推定性規則，新產品在銷售數據證明相反之前，都被假定為有獲利。
column5: presume 假定 + ive：先當作是真的來處理

column2: The bonus is contingent on meeting the annual sales target, so a poor year means no payment.
column3: 獎金取決於是否達成年度銷售目標，所以業績差的一年就沒有獎金。
column5: con 一起 + tingent 接觸：事情碰在一起才成立

column2: A good project manager keeps a contingency fund in case an unexpected delay raises costs.
column3: 好的專案經理會備有應急基金，以防意外延誤推高成本。
column5: contingent 取決於 + cy：萬一出事的備胎計畫

column2: A feasibility study found that opening a branch in the new district would be too costly to justify.
column3: 可行性研究發現，在新區開分店成本過高，不值得。
column5: feasible 可行 + ity：這件事做不做得成的程度

column2: Hiring fifty engineers in one month is hardly feasible given the current shortage of qualified candidates.
column3: 鑑於目前合格求職者短缺，一個月內聘到五十位工程師幾乎行不通。
column5: feas 像 feast 盛宴：這道菜真的端得上桌，做得成

column2: The board rejected the proposal as unfeasible, since it required technology that does not yet exist.
column3: 董事會以不可行為由拒絕了這項提案，因為它需要尚不存在的技術。
column4: an unfeasible plan (不可行的計畫)
column5: un 不 + feasible 可行：菜單上有，但廚房端不出來

column2: The cafe's profitability improved after it replaced expensive imported beans with a cheaper local supplier.
column3: 這家咖啡館改用較便宜的本地供應商取代昂貴的進口咖啡豆後，獲利能力提升了。
column5: profit 利潤 + ability：賺錢的本事有多強
column7: prof - it - a - bil - i - ty

column2: A profitable business earns more from its sales than it spends on running the company.
column3: 有利可圖的企業，從銷售賺到的錢比經營公司的花費更多。
column4: a profitable business (有獲利的事業)
column5: profit 利潤 + able：能把錢留進口袋的生意

column2: After three years of rising rent, the downtown shop became unprofitable and was finally closed.
column3: 租金連漲三年之後，這間市中心商店變得無利可圖，最後被關閉。
column5: un 不 + profitable：錢包只出不進

column2: The startup needs to sell ten thousand units a month to reach break-even and stop losing money.
column3: 這家新創公司每月須賣出一萬件才能達到損益兩平，停止虧損。
column5: break 打破 + even 平：收入剛好打平成本的那一刻
